subject: Data erasures roadmap and subprocessor transition
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healthcore.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthCore Legal <legal@healthcore.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T08:24:00Z
Subject: Data erasure roadmap & subprocessor transition for DPA

Hi Jonas,

Following our DPA review, legal has a couple of open items we need to lock down before we sign the amendment: backup purge timelines on subprocessor exit, log retention exceptions for EU workloads, and the mechanism for providing a certificate of deletion. Specifically:

- If Redwood terminates a subprocessor or a subprocessor relationship ends, how long are historical backups retained and where are they stored?
- Can we get a guarantee that EU production backups are cryptographically shredded (crypto-erase) after purge and a signed deletion certificate?
- Current logs are retained for 365 days — can we get a 180-day option for EU-regulated datasets?

We also need SOC 2 artifact access for the backup controls and a short runbook showing the steps for a subprocessor exit. Can you share a proposed timeline and any supporting docs?

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Privacy Operations
HealthCore Medical

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healthcore.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Data erasure roadmap & subprocessor transition for DPA

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Priyom (Infrastructure) to propose a technically-backed timeline and cert language — Laura, FYI for CS logistics.

High level answer up front: we support (1) isolated short-term retention for recovery on subprocessor exit, (2) crypto-erase for EU-designated backups on purge, and (3) configurable log retention tiers. Priyom, can you draft the runbook and manifest we can share? Kimberly, we'll need a short amendment clause and a deletion certificate template.

I’ll consolidate a single doc and timeline tomorrow. If HealthCore has a hard deadline for signature, please flag it.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healthcore.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Data erasure roadmap & subprocessor transition for DPA

Jonas/Team — attaching the technical artifacts as requested and a proposed operational timeline. Summary below; see attachments for runbook and manifest.

Proposed operational commitments (EU production):
- Backup retention (default): 90 days on primary S3 bucket.
- Subprocessor exit: when a subprocessor relationship ends, we snapshot relevant objects and move those snapshots to an isolated, access-restricted S3 bucket (geo-located per customer region). Snapshots are retained for an additional 30 days for recovery/transfer purposes, then securely deleted.
- Secure deletion method: for EU backups we will perform crypto-erase (crypto key destruction) and overwrite/deletion where applicable; we will produce a signed deletion certificate (template attached).
- Log retention: default 365 days; offer a 180-day retention tier for EU-regulated workloads on request. Implementation requires a config flag in the account settings and a 7-business-day lead time to propagate retention policies across long-term storage tiers.
- Exceptions: For legal hold or forensic preservation, we keep items on hold until release; legal hold overrides deletion schedule.

Timeline (from signing amendment):
T+0: Amendment signed and DPA addendum countersigned
T+2 business days: enable 180-day retention tier (if requested) and flag EU buckets for crypto-erase on next purge cycle
T+5 business days: create isolated snapshot store for any recent backups relevant to subprocessor exit
T+30 days: execute purge/crypto-erase of snapshots and submit deletion certificate to customer

Attachments (in thread): subprocessor_exit_runbook.pdf — runbook with exact S3 paths and CLI commands; s3_snapshot_manifest_20270502.csv — manifest of impacted prefixes for HealthCore; data_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx — mapping by data type and retention.

DocuSign link for the amendment: https://www.docusign.com/sign/HC-4521-amendment
Drive runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-subproc-runbooks

Happy to adjust timings if HealthCore needs faster turnaround.

—Priyom
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healthcore.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthCore Legal <legal@healthcore.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Data erasure roadmap & subprocessor transition for DPA

Thanks, Priyom — that level of detail helps. A couple of edits from legal:

- HealthCore requests the 180-day log retention be the default for EU production if the workload is classified as PHI/regulated. We can accept a 7-business-day lead time, but we want an SLA commitment to the enablement window.
- For the subprocessor snapshot purge, HealthCore requires the deletion certificate to include the crypto key identifiers and a proof-of-destruction statement.
- Can Redwood confirm whether any retained snapshots during the 30-day buffer are accessible to Redwood personnel other than the minimal infra on-call? We need to ensure an access log is generated and provided on request.

On timing: Legal needs the amendment countersigned by 2027-05-12 to align with an internal regulation audit. If you can get the signed addendum and certificate process finalized before then, we can proceed.

Best,
Elena

Elena — thanks for the feedback and the deadline. We’ll take the requested changes and produce: (1) an amendment redline with an SLA clause for the 7-business-day enablement window, (2) an updated deletion certificate template that includes the crypto key IDs and a signed proof-of-destruction statement, and (3) an access-log export template for snapshot access during the 30-day buffer.

Action items:
- Kimberly: prepare the redline and final amendment PDF for DocuSign by EOD 2027-05-04.
- Priyom: update runbook to include minimal personnel access and automated access logging; attach the updated manifest.
- Laura: please schedule a 30-minute kickoff with HealthCore for 2027-05-05 to walk the amendment and timeline (invite HealthCore legal + ops).

I’ve attached the deletion_certificate_template.docx for review. Once legal signs, we’ll initiate the config changes and start the sequence in the timeline above.

Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
